task: P0 briefing: root cause of "all agent prompts arrive as user" on Node 0 — harness defect, fix is one line per provider converter.
context:
P0 BRIEFING — I have a root-cause hypothesis for the Node 0 symptom you reported: all agent prompts arriving as `user`.

This is NOT a Node 0 config problem and NOT a prompt problem. It is inherited from the opencode harness binary itself, and it affects every node on the same version.

THE FINDING, IN ONE LINE: the harness marks synthetic messages and then ignores its own mark.

opencode v1.18.33, TaskTool.injectBackgroundResult:
  parts: [{ type: "text", synthetic: !0, text: Ur({...}) }]

`synthetic: true` IS persisted on the part and IS used by the TUI. It is not lost in storage. It is lost at the provider boundary — every provider converter branches on message role only:
  if (i.role === "user") { return { role: "user", content: ... } }
None of them read `synthetic`. On the wire, a subagent's summary is role:"user".

Worse: the one layer that DOES map it is inverted for our threat model.
  synthetic -> annotations.audience: ["assistant"]
That PROMOTES unknown provenance toward HIGHER authority. It should demote.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. Instruction Hierarchy (Weng/Heidecke/Beutel, OPENAI — not Anthropic, I had that wrong earlier — arXiv 2404.13208, ICLR 2025):
  System > User > Model output > Tool output   <- Tool output EXPLICITLY untrusted
A synthetic user message ranks ABOVE Tool Output. So a subagent that read hostile web content has its DISTILLED SUMMARY promoted above the authority of the raw material. The published hierarchy would call this a bug, not cover it.

FOUR FAILURE MODES TO CHECK AGAINST YOUR SYMPTOM:
  1. Scope collapse — quoted instructions from another agent treated as YOUR orders
  2. Reflexive compliance — text inside a report executed rather than reported
  3. Untraceable influence — behaviour changes with no visible cause
  4. Compounding — each nesting hop adds another synthetic-user surface
All four are UNAUDITABLE AFTER THE FACT. No published work addresses this.

WHAT DOES NOT WORK (all independently corroborated — do not spend time here):
  - Spotlighting/datamarking: BROKEN, ASR 1% -> >95% under adaptive attack
  - Prompt sandwiching: BROKEN, same paper
  - Prompt Guard 2 / DataSentinel: "fail to generalize to AgentDojo"
  - Sanitising the OUTPUT: insufficient; must sanitise BEFORE summarisation
  - Asking the subagent to rate itself: folklore, and the same defect class as a
    field the model fills in that the interface then accepts
Every mitigation with a proof or mechanism is HARNESS-SIDE. Every one requiring
model co-operation is FOLKLORE.

THE FIX — one line per provider converter, the bit already exists:
  // today: indistinguishable from a human turn
  parts: [{ type: "text", synthetic: true, text: payload }]
  // required: a role the hierarchy already ranks as untrusted
  parts: [{ type: "tool_result", toolName: "task", content: payload,
            annotations: { audience: ["assistant"], untrusted: true } }]

It works WITHOUT model cooperation: re-presenting a byte-identical claim under an
external role tag shifts correction rate by 23-93pp across seven model families
(arXiv 2606.05976), isolated as "addressability rather than verification" — the
model could always check the claim; it lacked a handle. The same result is the
attack: role relabelling alone changes behaviour without touching content, so any
content-based trust signal is orthogonal to what actually moves behaviour.

Defence in depth, only meaningful after the above: non-amplification invariant
(output_tier <= input_tier); egress-grounded provenance from RUNTIME telemetry
(network_fetch_count>0 => tainted — the runtime knows, the model cannot assert
otherwise); consumption gating; re-derivation from primary sources.

WHAT WE DO NOT KNOW, stated plainly:
  - No published defence targets agent-to-agent return provenance. The
    memory-laundering paper EXPLICITLY names inter-agent authority transfer as
    OUT OF SCOPE. This read direction is genuinely unstudied.
  - Enforcement is unimplemented; MCP says MUST, nothing checks.
  - WE HAVE NOT MEASURED YOUR NODE 0 INCIDENT. The mechanism is established and
    consistent with your symptom, but nobody has instrumented a real occurrence.
    Do not treat this as a closed case.

WHAT I NEED FROM YOU — three questions:
  1. Is the symptom ALL agent messages, or inter-agent only? Are handoff EVENTS
     affected, or only subagent task results? The mechanism I found covers subagent
     results. If federation events are ALSO arriving as user messages, that is a
     SECOND distinct code path and I have not found it.
  2. Does Node 0 run opencode 1.18.33? If the version differs, the converters may
     already be fixed and the problem is elsewhere.
  3. What did "real issues" look like in practice — scope collapse, reflexive
     compliance, or unexplained behaviour change? That tells us how urgent the fix is.
